relations.statement: Under reading L, admitted data (<a>, <ab>) are pairwise observationally collapsed: no admitted derivability profile distinguishes them.
relations.hypotheses: Reading L admits exactly (<a>, <ab>); no distinguishing instances admitted.

relations.statement: Under reading F, admitted data (<>, <a>, <ab>) are pairwise observationally collapsed: no admitted derivability profile distinguishes them.
relations.hypotheses: Reading F admits exactly (<>, <a>, <ab>); no distinguishing instances admitted.

lemmas.statement: For S(2) under readings L and F, every pair of admitted data is observationally collapsed relative to the source's derivability profiles; <ab> is not decomposed into a and b.
A collapsed pair is an active obstruction only when a supplied question or separation requirement demands different answers on it.

near_misses.claim: The flat grammar sn.ebnf parsing <ab> as a pair of glyphs shows the source decomposes <ab> into a and b.
near_misses.rejecting_invariant: sn.ebnf is a later interpretation with its own parser; the source S(2) keeps <ab> opaque.

near_misses.claim: A two-vertex graph or permutation representation of the pair (S2Collapse) is an admitted directed relation in the source.
near_misses.rejecting_invariant: Such a representation is declared structure, not an admitted relation.

near_misses.claim: Collapse of an admitted pair alone is an active obstruction, giving s2 = 1.
near_misses.rejecting_invariant: s2 = 1 requires a supplied separation demand; collapse alone is not an obstruction.
